# Command reference

The text below is what the binary prints for `--help`, for the top-level command
and for each subcommand. The [command-line overview](overview.md) explains how
the commands fit together.

## `vibegraph`

```text
Toy leading-order Monte-Carlo event generator

Usage: vibegraph [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  integrate     Integrate the cross section of a process, saving the adapted VEGAS grids
  generate      Generate an unweighted event sample from a saved grid, as a Les Houches file
  check-events  Read a Les Houches file back and check that it is internally consistent
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --no-network
          Never download anything; a missing asset becomes a refusal stating the URL, size and checksum it would have fetched. `$VIBEGRAPH_NO_NETWORK`, set to any value, does the same for a whole environment, and either one outranks `--yes`

  -y, --yes
          Answer yes to any "may I download this?" question instead of asking. Needed to fetch an asset from a script, a CI job, or anything else with no terminal, where the default is to refuse

  -v, --verbose...
          Raise the level: `-v` run notices, `-vv` pipeline internals, `-vvv` all

  -q, --quiet
          Report only warnings and errors

      --log-level <LEVEL>
          Report at this level, instead of counting `-v`s
          
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

      --log-file <PATH>
          Also record every event, at `trace`, to this file.
          
          The file is written whatever the terminal is showing, which is what makes a run reviewable afterwards at a level nobody chose to watch it at.

      --tui
          Draw the live status pane even where one would not be drawn by default

      --no-tui
          Never draw the live status pane; report in plain lines

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `vibegraph integrate`

```text
Integrate the cross section of a process, saving the adapted VEGAS grids

Usage: vibegraph integrate [OPTIONS] <PROC_CARD>

Arguments:
  <PROC_CARD>
          Process card selecting the model and process (`import model` + `generate`); `-` reads the card from stdin

Options:
      --run-card <RUN_CARD>
          MadGraph `run_card.dat`; absent → MadGraph LO defaults

      --param-card <PARAM_CARD>
          SLHA `param_card.dat` to evaluate the model at; absent → the model's defaults under its restriction. The artifact records every parameter the card moves, and `generate` evaluates at those values. Refused: a width given as `Auto`, a non-zero value for a parameter the restriction fixed to zero, a value other than one for a parameter it fixed to one, a move that splits parameters the restriction merged, and an entry the model has no parameter for. A mass or width the model computes (MW in the SM) is ignored, with a warning when it disagrees

      --out <OUT>
          Output directory for the grid artifact (`<out>/grid.bin.zst`)
          
          [default: .]

      --force
          Overwrite an existing artifact

      --no-network
          Never download anything; a missing asset becomes a refusal stating the URL, size and checksum it would have fetched. `$VIBEGRAPH_NO_NETWORK`, set to any value, does the same for a whole environment, and either one outranks `--yes`

      --ufo-dir <UFO_DIR>
          Directory containing the proc card's UFO model directory; defaults to `$VIBEGRAPH_UFO_DIR`, then the `~/.vibegraph` cache, then the current directory. Unused for the built-in Standard Model

  -y, --yes
          Answer yes to any "may I download this?" question instead of asking. Needed to fetch an asset from a script, a CI job, or anything else with no terminal, where the default is to refuse

      --neval <NEVAL>
          VEGAS evaluations per adaptation iteration.
          
          Split across the channels by their selection weights, but every channel draws at least 512 points so none stops covering its own region: a process with many channels spends `512 × channels` per iteration however small this is. Also sets the α-survey's points per iteration, clamped to `[10000, 40000]`.
          
          [default: 120000]

  -v, --verbose...
          Raise the level: `-v` run notices, `-vv` pipeline internals, `-vvv` all

      --niter <NITER>
          VEGAS adaptation iterations under `--fixed-budget`. The default convergence mode decides its own iteration count, capped by `--max-iters`
          
          [default: 12]

  -q, --quiet
          Report only warnings and errors

      --log-level <LEVEL>
          Report at this level, instead of counting `-v`s
          
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

      --target-rel <REL>
          Integrate until σ's relative uncertainty reaches this.
          
          The uncertainty the stop reads is the quoted one with each channel's variance widened to the scatter its iterations actually show, where that is larger, so a run whose iterations disagree by more than their error bars keeps going. `--neval` sets the points an iteration spends; how many iterations run is what the target decides, bounded by `--min-iters`, `--max-iters` and `--max-points`.
          
          [default: 0.001]

      --fixed-budget
          Spend a fixed `--neval × --niter` and stop, instead of converging to `--target-rel`.
          
          The mode a banked run is reproducible under: a fixed budget draws the same points from the same seed every time, where a convergence run's length depends on the variance it measures.

      --log-file <PATH>
          Also record every event, at `trace`, to this file.
          
          The file is written whatever the terminal is showing, which is what makes a run reviewable afterwards at a level nobody chose to watch it at.

      --min-iters <MIN_ITERS>
          Iterations that must run before the convergence target may stop a run
          
          [default: 6]

      --tui
          Draw the live status pane even where one would not be drawn by default

      --max-iters <MAX_ITERS>
          Iteration cap for `--target-rel`.
          
          A safety bound, not a budget: a run that reaches its target stops there, so the cap only ever binds on a run whose iterations keep disagreeing. Sized so that the widest gated process needing ~156 iterations at the default `--neval` converges with headroom; `--max-points` still bounds the total spend.
          
          [default: 500]

      --no-tui
          Never draw the live status pane; report in plain lines

      --max-points <MAX_POINTS>
          Evaluation cap for `--target-rel`, over all channels and iterations
          
          [default: 400000000]

      --allocate <ALLOCATE>
          How the per-iteration budget is split across channels.
          
          Defaults to `by-alpha` under `--fixed-budget` — the split a banked run is reproducible under — and to `neyman` under a convergence target, where it reaches the same accuracy in somewhat fewer evaluations on a multichannel process (`p p > l+ l- j`, 6 channels, 20 seeds: 1.49M evaluations against 1.58M at a 0.179% target, the same σ) and is the same run on a single-channel one (`p p > e+ e-`).

          Possible values:
          - by-alpha: `Nⱼ ∝ αⱼ`, the split the channel weights imply
          - neyman:   Neyman: `Nⱼ ∝ αⱼ σⱼ`, driven by the variance each channel measures

      --seed <SEED>
          RNG seed for the integration; defaults to the run card's `iseed` when it is not 0, and to 20260719 otherwise. The seed used is recorded in the artifact

  -j, --parallel <N>
          Worker threads (default: one per core). Results do not depend on it: any thread count produces byte-identical output

      --parallel-diagrams
          Enumerate diagrams on the worker pool too, instead of on one thread. Pays off only for processes whose enumeration costs seconds; below that the fan-out is a slowdown. Timing only: the artifact is identical either way

      --map-split-angle <SPLIT_ANGLE>
          How each 2-body split of the decay tree draws its decay angle.
          
          Every choice is a parametrisation of the same phase space — none moves the cross section, only the evaluations needed to reach an accuracy. `auto` is `soft-all`, which measures half the evaluations of `isotropic` on `p p > l+ l- j`, 0.85× on `g u > e+ e- u` and 0.67× on `u u~ > g g g`, where every moving split has a gluon daughter and it is the `soft-emission` map. On a `2 → 2` process no split moves and every choice is the same map. The choice is recorded in the artifact and replayed by `vibegraph generate`.

          Possible values:
          - auto:          `soft-all`
          - isotropic:     Flat in `cos θ` and `φ` against the collision-CM axes
          - windowed:      Flat in `cos θ*` from the parent's flight direction, confined to the window the cut-implied energy floors admit, on every split
          - soft-emission: Density `∝ 1/(E₁E₂)` — a splitting kernel's `1/(z(1−z))` — on the splits with a single gluon or photon daughter
          - soft-all:      The `1/(E₁E₂)` map on every split
          
          [default: auto]

      --map-tau <TAU>
          How a proton-beam run draws `τ = ŝ/s` above the cut-implied minimum.
          
          `auto` is MadEvent's rule: `inverse-square` unless a finite-width resonance spans the whole final state, and `log` where one does. `inverse-square` measures better where it applies (0.77× the evaluations on `p p > j j`, 0.65× on `p p > b b~`) and worse on Drell–Yan (1.06×), where the resonance's peak sits in the `τ` draw.

          Possible values:
          - auto:           `inverse-square`, or `log` where a resonance spans the whole final state
          - log:            Density `∝ 1/τ` above the cut-implied `τ_min`
          - inverse-square: Density `∝ 1/τ²`, MadEvent's map for a hadronic run with no resonance spanning the whole final state
          
          [default: auto]

      --map-rung-order <RUNG_ORDER>
          The order a peripheral (t-channel) chain draws its rungs in.
          
          `auto` is `derived`; `reversed` reads 1.01 ± 0.02 of it on `u u~ > g g g`.

          Possible values:
          - auto
          - derived:  Outward from beam 0, as the diagram's spacelike lines nest
          - reversed: The same rungs in reverse — a control, not a recommendation
          
          [default: auto]

      --map-pair-order <PAIR_ORDER>
          The order a split whose two daughters both carry a finite-width resonance draws their invariants in.
          
          `auto` is `symmetric`: either daughter first with probability ½. `ordered` draws one daughter on its pole first, which below the two poles' sum (`H → ZZ*`) leaves the half of the peak with the other daughter on shell in a Breit–Wigner tail.

          Possible values:
          - auto
          - ordered:   The left daughter first, on its pole
          - symmetric: Either daughter first with probability ½
          
          [default: auto]

      --grid-bin-weight <BIN_WEIGHT>
          What each point adds to its bins of the refinement histogram

          Possible values:
          - squared:  The point's squared weight `(f·w)²`
          - absolute: The point's weight `|f·w|`, as MadEvent accumulates it
          
          [default: squared]

      --grid-acceptance-rescale
          Credit each bin with the mean of its accepted points: multiply its histogram entry by the iteration's accepted points over the bin's, capped at 10⁴, as MadEvent does while its grid adapts

      --grid-max-bin-width <K>
          Bound every refined bin's width at this multiple of the uniform width, which must exceed 1; `none` leaves the width unbounded
          
          [default: 6]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `vibegraph generate`

```text
Generate an unweighted event sample from a saved grid, as a Les Houches file

Usage: vibegraph generate [OPTIONS] <ARTIFACT>

Arguments:
  <ARTIFACT>
          Grid artifact from a completed `vibegraph integrate` run

Options:
      --seed <SEED>
          RNG seed for the generation; required. Same artifact, settings and seed, same sample, so each generation job from one grid needs its own seed

      --nevents <NEVENTS>
          Events to write; defaults to the `nevents` the artifact recorded

  -o, --out <OUT>
          Output Les Houches file
          
          [default: events.lhe]

      --force
          Overwrite an existing event file

      --no-network
          Never download anything; a missing asset becomes a refusal stating the URL, size and checksum it would have fetched. `$VIBEGRAPH_NO_NETWORK`, set to any value, does the same for a whole environment, and either one outranks `--yes`

      --strategy <STRATEGY>
          Weight strategy

          Possible values:
          - buffer:              Hold the sample, write the weights (`IDWTUP = -4`, or `-3` under `event_norm = sum` or `unity`)
          - stochastic-rounding: Stream, writing each event `floor(w) + Bernoulli(frac(w))` times at unit weight (`IDWTUP = +3`)
          
          [default: buffer]

  -y, --yes
          Answer yes to any "may I download this?" question instead of asking. Needed to fetch an asset from a script, a CI job, or anything else with no terminal, where the default is to refuse

      --event-norm <EVENT_NORM>
          How the written weights are normalised; defaults to the `event_norm` the artifact recorded. It moves the weights and the `<init>` block, not the events drawn

          Possible values:
          - average: The weights' mean is the cross section (`IDWTUP = -4`)
          - sum:     The weights' sum is the cross section (`IDWTUP = -3`)
          - unity:   Every weight is one (`IDWTUP = -3`)

  -v, --verbose...
          Raise the level: `-v` run notices, `-vv` pipeline internals, `-vvv` all

  -q, --quiet
          Report only warnings and errors

      --ufo-dir <UFO_DIR>
          Directory containing the recorded proc card's UFO model directory; defaults to `$VIBEGRAPH_UFO_DIR`, then the `~/.vibegraph` cache, then the current directory. Unused for the built-in Standard Model. The model found must be the one the artifact was integrated against

      --log-level <LEVEL>
          Report at this level, instead of counting `-v`s
          
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

      --scan-points <N|share>
          Points the frozen `w_max` scan spends on *each* channel, or `share` to give every channel the integration's own per-channel budget instead. What the budget buys depends on `--max-truncation`: at zero a larger budget raises the maxima, trading acceptance for fewer events above them; under a truncation it sharpens the quantile the maxima converge to
          
          [default: share]

      --log-file <PATH>
          Also record every event, at `trace`, to this file.
          
          The file is written whatever the terminal is showing, which is what makes a run reviewable afterwards at a level nobody chose to watch it at.

      --max-truncation <SHARE>
          Share of each channel's scanned cross section its maximum may leave above itself. `0` takes the largest weight the scan saw instead; a larger share lowers the maxima, accepting more trials and giving more of the accepted events a weight above one
          
          [default: 0.01]

      --reweight-card <REWEIGHT_CARD>
          MadGraph reweight card: every event also carries its weight under each `launch` block's parameters, as an LHEF `<rwgt>` block

      --tui
          Draw the live status pane even where one would not be drawn by default

      --no-tui
          Never draw the live status pane; report in plain lines

      --reweight-exact
          Evaluate every reweighting hypothesis directly, never through a polynomial in the couplings. Slower; for cross-checking

      --reweight-couplings <NAME,...>
          Track the amplitude as a polynomial jointly in these external parameters (comma-separated names), so every hypothesis costs a quadratic form rather than an amplitude evaluation: an event costs one evaluation per monomial of the amplitude — `1 + n` for `n` couplings entering at most once per diagram — whatever the number of hypotheses. The card may then move only these, and each must enter every subprocess polynomially

  -j, --parallel <N>
          Worker threads (default: one per core). Results do not depend on it: any thread count produces byte-identical output

      --parallel-diagrams
          Enumerate diagrams on the worker pool too, instead of on one thread. Pays off only for processes whose enumeration costs seconds; below that the fan-out is a slowdown. Timing only: the artifact is identical either way

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `vibegraph check-events`

```text
Read a Les Houches file back and check that it is internally consistent

Usage: vibegraph check-events [OPTIONS] <EVENTS>

Arguments:
  <EVENTS>
          Les Houches file to read back

Options:
      --tolerance <TOLERANCE>
          Relative tolerance for momentum conservation and mass shells
          
          [default: 0.000001]

      --min-events <MIN_EVENTS>
          Fail unless the file holds at least this many events

      --no-network
          Never download anything; a missing asset becomes a refusal stating the URL, size and checksum it would have fetched. `$VIBEGRAPH_NO_NETWORK`, set to any value, does the same for a whole environment, and either one outranks `--yes`

  -y, --yes
          Answer yes to any "may I download this?" question instead of asking. Needed to fetch an asset from a script, a CI job, or anything else with no terminal, where the default is to refuse

  -v, --verbose...
          Raise the level: `-v` run notices, `-vv` pipeline internals, `-vvv` all

  -q, --quiet
          Report only warnings and errors

      --log-level <LEVEL>
          Report at this level, instead of counting `-v`s
          
          [possible values: off, error, warn, info, debug, trace]

      --log-file <PATH>
          Also record every event, at `trace`, to this file.
          
          The file is written whatever the terminal is showing, which is what makes a run reviewable afterwards at a level nobody chose to watch it at.

      --tui
          Draw the live status pane even where one would not be drawn by default

      --no-tui
          Never draw the live status pane; report in plain lines

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
